content: Telogen effluvium is a condition characterized by sudden and widespread hair loss, which occurs due to a disruption in the normal hair growth cycle. Causes This disruption is frequently triggered by a traumatic event, such as undergoing chemotherapy, childbirth, puberty, major surgical procedures, severe psychological or physical stress, or chronic illnesses of significant severity. These stressors cause a large number of hair follicles to prematurely enter the telogen phase, which is the resting stage of the hair growth cycle. After approximately three months in the telogen phase, the affected follicles transition into the anagen phase, which is the active growth stage. During this process, new hair begins to form beneath the old hair, pushing the old hair out of the follicle. This results in a period of diffuse hair shedding. In most cases, telogen effluvium is self-limiting and resolves on its own. It can affect individuals of any age group. Classification There is also a chronic form of telogen effluvium, which is essentially the same condition but persists over a longer period of time without spontaneous resolution. Presentation in Pregnancy A common example of telogen effluvium occurs in women after pregnancy. In this scenario, significant hair loss is observed a few months postpartum, as the protective effects of elevated estrogen levels during pregnancy are withdrawn. This postpartum shedding typically resolves spontaneously, and hair regrowth usually begins within three months.
